note: Masonry Views provides a single Views style plugin (@ViewsStyle id 'masonry', theme views_view_masonry) selected as a view display's Format. It delegates layout options and rendering to the required masonry module's masonry.service. Configuration lives entirely in the view display's display_options.style ({type: masonry, options: {gutterWidth, layoutColumnWidth, isLayoutResizable, ...}}). No config page, permissions, schema, or Drush. Introspection reads the style options of a live masonry-style view; execution switches a view's Format to masonry and sets a masonry layout option, both verified against the live views.view config entity.

evals.prompt: How do I display a Drupal View's results as a masonry grid using the masonry_views module? What do I change on the view?
evals.expected_output: Set the view display's Format (style plugin) to 'Masonry' (plugin id 'masonry'). It renders results via the views_view_masonry theme hook, wrapping each row as a .masonry-item inside a .masonry-layout-<view-id> container.

evals.prompt: What does masonry_views depend on to actually lay out the grid, and what happens if the jQuery Masonry library is missing?
evals.expected_output: It requires the separate 'masonry' module (>= 4.x) and its jQuery Masonry library; masonry_views delegates options and rendering to masonry.service. Without the library the options form is disabled ('These options have been disabled as the jQuery Masonry plugin is not installed.') and no layout JS is attached.

evals.prompt: Which theme hook and CSS classes does masonry_views use to render items, so I can target them with CSS?
evals.expected_output: Theme hook views_view_masonry (template views-view-masonry.html.twig). Each row is wrapped in a div with class 'masonry-item', inside a container with class 'masonry-layout-<view-id>' (and 'masonry-group-<n>' when grouping); the rows container also carries data-drupal-masonry-layout.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view named 'masonry_views_probe' that uses the Masonry style. Inspect its live configuration and state the configured gutter width (gutterWidth) value.
On this Drupal site, inspect the view named 'masonry_views_probe' and state which Views style (format) plugin its default display uses.
evals.expected_output: Its default display uses the 'masonry' style plugin (display_options.style.type = masonry).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view with machine name 'masonry_views_task' whose default display currently uses the plain unformatted style. Change its Format to the Masonry style provided by masonry_views, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The masonry_views_task view's default display display_options.style.type is set to 'masonry' (via the Views UI Format setting, or by editing the view config).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view with machine name 'masonry_views_gutter' that already uses the Masonry style. Configure its masonry layout so the gutter width (gutterWidth) between items is 20, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The masonry_views_gutter view's default display style options gutterWidth is set to 20 (display_options.style.options.gutterWidth = '20').
